cases.task: Design only: a single-process two-thread deadline scheduler has up to 8000 active tasks and about 5 million durable historical records. Existing dispatch scans/filters/sorts a shared list and returns mutable row references; cancel scans and unconditionally changes state. Due tasks must be claimed in stable (due_at, job_id) order. Successful cancellation prevents a later claim; cancellation of a started task returns already_started. Recover after restart. Target scheduling-decision p95 is 10ms, excluding task execution. Do not modify execution code or claim the target has been measured.
acceptance: Separates active and historical scale and compares plausible representations with stated operation/memory assumptions
Defines claim/cancellation semantics, ownership, durable commit boundary and consistency of derived indexes
Addresses recovery, uncertain outcomes and external execution identity without promising universal exactly-once effects
Specifies realistic correctness, concurrency, recovery, resource-growth and comparable performance checks
Keeps the existing stack as a candidate, preserves design-only scope and does not invent measured latency
